name: DISA STIG, SSH server (Amazon Linux 2023)
reference: CIS Amazon Linux 2023 STIG Benchmark v1.0.0, the SSH rules requiring FIPS 140-2/140-3-validated ciphers and MACs (verified against /etc/crypto-policies/back-ends/opensshserver.config). Each audit fails a server whose configuration lists anything other than the named list, so this profile is an allowlist of those two lists.
summary: The US Department of Defense hardening for SSH on Amazon Linux 2023: a FIPS allowlist of ciphers and MACs set through the system crypto-policies. Its mandated lists coincide with the RHEL 9 STIG's -- but this is the Amazon Linux 2023 document, cited and versioned on its own.
notes: One profile per STIG document. Amazon Linux 2023 configures SSH crypto through /etc/crypto-policies/back-ends/opensshserver.config rather than a plain Ciphers/MACs line in sshd_config, but that is only how the list is set; what this tool measures is what the server offers on the wire, which is what the allowlist governs. Its mandated cipher and MAC lists coincide with the RHEL 9 STIG's (ciphers aes256-gcm@openssh.com, aes256-ctr, aes128-gcm@openssh.com, aes128-ctr; MACs the four HMAC-SHA-2 in plain and encrypt-then-MAC form), reflecting the shared RHEL crypto-policy lineage, but it is a distinct document, so a distinct profile. It states no key-exchange rule, so this profile constrains ciphers and MACs only. Lists taken from audit/remediation, not Default Value.

cipher.reason: The Amazon Linux 2023 STIG cipher rule's audit fails a server offering anything other than these four; the remediation sets exactly them.

mac.reason: The Amazon Linux 2023 STIG MAC rule's audit fails a server offering anything other than these four FIPS-validated MACs.
